violation_type.title: Medication Authorization - Parent May Not Authorize in Excess of Label Directions or Child's Health-Care Professional Directions (26 TAC §746.3803(c))
violation_type.short_title: Medication Authorization - Parent May Not Authorize in Excess of Label Directions or Child's Health-Care Professional Directions
violation_type.typical_finding: The operation has mediation authorization forms that signed by parents that exceed label directions and authorization forms for mediation not to be used by "said" age group.

finding_variants.text: The operation has mediation authorization forms that signed by parents that exceed label directions and authorization forms for mediation not to be used by "said" age group.
There was a bottle of tylenol for an infant that did not have doctor instructions.

Medication was left at the operation for children that did not follow the label instructions for the child's age range.        *This was corrected at inspection when the medication was removed and sent home.

2 children have over the counter medication stored at the operation without a doctor's note and the parents have instructed in excess of the label as the labels instruct to ask a doctor for dosage per their age.

At the time of the inspection a parent had authorized a dosage of medication that exceeded what the label stipulates the dosage to be based on the child's age. The medication had been administered twice.
A parent instructed the operation to administer 2mL of benedryl when the label states to not use unless directed by a doctor for the age of the child.

Medication Authorization - Parent May Not Authorize in Excess of Label Directions or Child's Health-Care Professional Directions: A 22 month old child in care was administered .62 ML more of a dosage of ibuprofen than what was directed on the medication's label for the child's age, per the parents request.     This was corrected at inspection when the operation made a change in policy and sent a mass email to all enrolled parents stating that the operation will no longer administer medication effective 4/24/2024.
